display_name: James of Pharatha, companion of Azas

names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 10 Απριλίου, «Άγιοι Ιάκωβος ο Πρεσβύτερος και Αζάς ο Διάκονος», with the rank word and the order left off.

Read out of the title on the name link behind his place in the line for 10 апреля ст. ст., name page 880, «Иаков Персидский, пресвитер, сщмч.», with the office word and the rank abbreviation left off. **The bare «Иаков» was refused**: it is the `ru` form `james-martyr-1937`, `james-presbyter-martyr-1937` and `james-son-of-alphaeus` hold between them, and the gate already prints that fold unread, so storing it would have widened it to four. This calendar gives him Персидский where saint.gr gives him the village of Pharatha, and the two epithets are not the same claim: `.tmp/foldchk.py` reports no folder holding the stored form and `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` reports it as a key no other folder holds.

death.note: **Two calendars, two years, forty-eight years apart, and the interval carries both.** days.pravoslavie.ru closes its day line for 10 апреля ст. ст. with «(ок. 380)» and its life opens «Святые мученики Иаков пресвитер и диаконы Азадан и Авдикий скончались в Персии при царе Сапоре около 380 года» — about the year 380, under a king Shapur it does not number. saint.gr dates the same arrest «Καταγγέλθηκαν (332 μ.Χ.) σαν χριστιανοί», denounced as Christians in 332, and names the king: «Σαπώρ Β΄», whose reign ends in 379, so the Greek year falls inside a reign the Russian year falls just outside. **A third thing read pulls the same way as the Russian year and is not a year**: the Russian life says the three were taken «вместе с епископом Акепсимом», with the bishop Acepsimas, whose own folder this corpus dates 376. Neither year is chosen. Read 6 October 2026.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 10 апреля ст. ст. — «Мчч. Иакова пресвитера, Азадана и Авдикия диаконов, Персидских (ок. 380).»

attestations.note: Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 10ης Απριλίου — «Άγιοι Ιάκωβος ο Πρεσβύτερος και Αζάς ο Διάκονος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 10 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and heads both men «(; - 332)». Two names in one line, so two folders. Pharatha is the village the page gives him — «Ο πρεσβύτερος Ιάκωβος ήταν από το χωριό Φαραθά» — and it is in the display name because the corpus holds a dozen other men of this name; he is not the great-martyr James the Persian, whom the corpus keeps on the Romanian 27 November. The page gives two spellings for the chief magus who tried them, «Αχοσχαργάν (ή Αρχωγαϊχάρ)», and prints no hymn.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
